Name: Help Wanted - Together
Author: semper1dem
Description:
[center][size=5][b]Help Wanted — Together[/b][/size]
[i]A multiplayer-compatible rewrite of aedenthorn's Help Wanted mod[/i][/center]

[line]

[size=4][b]Overview[/b][/size]

[b]Help Wanted — Together[/b] transforms the Help Wanted board into a richer, more dynamic experience. Up to six colour-coded quest notes appear on the board each day — item deliveries, resource collections, fishing targets, and monster slaying — each showing a miniature NPC portrait. The mod is a full rewrite of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2644]aedenthorn's original Help Wanted[/url], rebuilt from the ground up with working multiplayer support and a set of new mechanics that scale with your farm and your party.

[line]

[size=4][b]Credits[/b][/size]

Original concept and design by [b]aedenthorn[/b]. This fork was created because the original mod had fundamental multiplayer desynchronisation issues that could not be fixed with a simple patch — the quest board state was never shared between players, and two farmers could accept the same quest simultaneously. This version reimplements the core systems with multiplayer as a first-class concern.

[line]
[b][size=4]Important[/size]

[/b]I had to rewrite parts of this mod so I'm unsure whether or not all crashes are captured and safely handled since vanilla quest building logic is weird and I'm too silly.

In some cases this may result in day not saving when going to sleep, this is why I advise to use [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/26194]QuickSave[/url] before going to sleep so you don't lose progress.

[line]


[size=4][b]What's New in This Fork[/b][/size]

[size=3][b]Multiplayer Support[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

The entire quest lifecycle is now synchronised across all players in a co-op session.

[list]
[*]The host (master game) generates and owns the quest board. Quests are broadcast to all connected clients on day start.[/*]
[*]When a farmhand joins a session, their client automatically requests the current board state from the host.[/*]
[*]Quest acceptance is routed through the host to prevent race conditions — two players cannot accept the same quest.[/*]
[*]If a quest is taken while another player is viewing it, their board updates immediately and the selection is cleared safely.[/*]
[/list]
[size=3][b]Average Quest Count[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

Instead of a flat maximum, the board now targets a configurable [b]Average Quests[/b] count. The actual number varies each day around that average (up to the configured maximum), so the board feels alive rather than always full.

[size=3][b]Avoid Pending Accepted Quests[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

When enabled, the board will not post a quest whose [i]type + NPC + objective[/i] is already present in [i]any[/i] farmer's active quest log. In multiplayer this checks all connected players, preventing the board from repeating a quest your co-op partner is still working on.

[size=3][b]Kill Count Variance[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

Slay Monster quests receive a random ±N adjustment to the kill count so they don't feel repetitive.

[size=3][b]Scale to Average Combat Level[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

Slay Monster quest kill counts [i]and[/i] rewards scale based on the average combat level across all players (range: 0.75× at level 0 → 1.75× at level 10). Makes late-game monster quests appropriately challenging and rewarding without manual tuning, and adapts automatically in multiplayer.

[size=3][b]Reward Variance[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

A configurable random ±% is applied to every quest reward, so identical quests don't always pay the same amount.

[size=3][b]Scale Reward to Friendship[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

Quest rewards scale from 1× (no friendship) up to 2× (maximum hearts) based on your average friendship with the requesting NPC. In multiplayer, the average friendship across all farmers is used.

[size=3][b]Avoid Duplicate Objectives[/b][/size] [color=#ffcc00][b][NEW][/b][/color]

The board will not post the same NPC + objective combination twice on the same day, even if quest type weights are heavily skewed.

[line]

[size=4][b]Features Carried Over from aedenthorn's Version[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Multiple daily quests[/b] — configurable maximum quest count per day.[/*]
[*][b]Colour-coded quest notes[/b] — yellow (item delivery), green (resource collection), red (slay monster), blue (fishing) — colour-matched pin and pad per quest type.[/*]
[*][b]NPC portraits on notes[/b] — a tinted NPC portrait appears on each note; tint colour and position are configurable.[/*]
[*][b]Custom pad/pin textures via Content Patcher[/b] — target-specific and quest-type-specific texture overrides (e.g. a different note style for Linus or for fishing quests).[/*]
[*][b]Item delivery filtering[/b] — restrict quests to only items the NPC [i]likes[/i] or [i]loves[/i], with an option to require loved gifts only.[/*]
[*][b]Scale price to earnings[/b] — prevents high-value item quests from appearing until the player has earned enough money.[/*]
[*][b]Max item price cap[/b] — hard upper limit on requested item value.[/*]
[*][b]Artisan goods toggle[/b] — include or exclude artisan goods from item delivery quests.[/*]
[*][b]Ignore vanilla item selection[/b] — fully overrides the game's item picker rather than just filtering its output.[/*]
[*][b]Quest type weights[/b] — set the relative probability of each quest type appearing.[/*]
[*][b]One quest per villager[/b] — the same NPC will not appear twice on the board in one day.[/*]
[*][b]Quest deadline control[/b] — configurable base days to complete plus random variance.[/*]
[*][b]Note appearance[/b] — scale, overlap thresholds, portrait offset, and portrait tint are all configurable.[/*]
[*][b]Custom quest JSON packs[/b] — other mods (or your own Content Patcher pack) can inject fully custom quests onto the board. See the [i]Custom Quests[/i] section below.[/*]
[/list]
[size=3][b]Known Limitations[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Avoid Max Hearts[/b] — the option to skip NPCs you are already at max friendship with [i]only works in single-player[/i]. In multiplayer it is automatically disabled because friendship levels differ per farmer and no single-player perspective can be used.[/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]Configuration[/b][/size]

All settings are available in [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] or by editing
[code]config.json[/code]in the mod folder.


Mod Enabled (default: true)
    Master toggle.

Max Quests (default: 6)
    Maximum quests on the board per day.

Average Quests (default: 3)
    Target average quest count; day-to-day count varies around this.

One Quest / Villager (default: true)
    Each NPC appears at most once per day.

Avoid Duplicate Objectives (default: true)
    No two quests with the same NPC + objective.

Avoid Pending Accepted Quests (default: true)
    Skip quests already in any farmer's quest log.

Avoid Max Heart Villagers (default: true)
    Skip NPCs at max hearts (single-player only).

Days To Complete (default: 2)
    Base deadline in days.

Days Variance (default: 3)
    Random extra days added to deadline.

Restrict To Preferred Items (default: true)
    Item delivery quests use liked/loved gifts only.

Only Loved Items (default: false)
    Exclude liked gifts; only loved gifts qualify.

Allow Artisan Goods (default: true)
    Artisan goods can appear in item delivery quests.

Scale Price To Earnings (default: true)
    Gates expensive quests behind player earnings.

Earnings Percent (default: 0.02)
    Item value cap as fraction of total earnings.

Max Item Price (default: -1)
    Hard item price cap (-1 = disabled).

Scale Reward To Friendship (default: true)
    Reward scales 1×–2× with NPC friendship.

Reward Variance (default: 0.1)
    Random ±10% applied to reward.

Kill Count Variance (default: 3)
    Random ±N applied to slay monster kill count.

Scale To Avg Combat Level (default: true)
    Slay quests scale with average party combat level.

Item Delivery Weight (default: 40)
    Relative probability for item delivery quests.

Resource Collect Weight (default: 30)
    Relative probability for resource collection quests.

Slay Monster Weight (default: 30)
    Relative probability for slay monster quests.

Fishing Weight (default: 30)
    Relative probability for fishing quests.

[size=4][b]Custom Quests via Content Patcher[/b][/size]

Other mods can inject custom quests onto the Help Wanted board by editing the
[code]aedenthorn.HelpWanted/dictionary[/code]asset. Each entry is a [b]QuestNoteTemplate[/b].

[size=3][b]Example 1 — Item Delivery Quest[/b][/size]

Penny asks for a Melon. Uses default note appearance for item delivery (yellow pad).

[code]
{
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "EditData",
      "Target": "aedenthorn.HelpWanted/dictionary",
      "Entries": {
        "MyMod.PennyMelonQuest": {
          "weight": 50,
          "quest": {
            "questType": "ItemDelivery",
            "questTitle": "Penny's Request",
            "questDescription": "Penny stopped by the shop asking if anyone had a spare Melon. She seemed embarrassed to ask directly.",
            "currentObjective": "Bring a Melon to Penny.",
            "target": "Penny",
            "targetMessage": "Oh! You actually brought one? Thank you so much!",
            "itemId": "254",
            "reward": 400
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}[/code]
[size=3][b]Example 2 — Slay Monster Quest[/b][/size]

Clint wants Slimes killed. The
[code]itemId[/code]field holds the monster name for slay quests. Kill count variance and combat scaling from config still apply on top of the base
[code]number[/code].

[code]
{
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "EditData",
      "Target": "aedenthorn.HelpWanted/dictionary",
      "Entries": {
        "MyMod.ClintSlimeQuest": {
          "weight": 30,
          "quest": {
            "questType": "SlayMonster",
            "questTitle": "Slime Problem",
            "questDescription": "Clint has been complaining that Green Slimes are getting too close to the mines entrance. He's offering a reward to anyone willing to clear some out.",
            "currentObjective": "Slay 0/8 Green Slimes.",
            "target": "Clint",
            "targetMessage": "Good work. Those things were getting on my nerves.",
            "itemId": "Green Slime",
            "number": 8,
            "reward": 600
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}[/code]

[size=4][b]Texture Lookup Order[/b][/size]

For default (non-custom) quests, textures are resolved in priority order:

[code]
aedenthorn.HelpWanted/pad/{NpcName}/{QuestType}   <- most specific
aedenthorn.HelpWanted/pad/{NpcName}
aedenthorn.HelpWanted/pad/{QuestType}
aedenthorn.HelpWanted/pad                         <- global default[/code]
The same order applies for
[code]pin[/code]textures. Numbered variants (
[code]/pad/1[/code],
[code]/pad/2[/code], …) are loaded and one is chosen randomly.
